1.title: アイウエオ・カキクケコ

kana.intro: Katakana are the same sounds as hiragana, written another way. They are used for words from other languages, and for names.

cards.note: a, the same sound as あ.
A long line ー makes the sound before it long: ケーキ kēki, a cake. Katakana words use it where hiragana write a second vowel.

drill.label: Read the kana
why: ア is a, the same sound as あ.

drill.label: Pick the kana you hear
why: ク is ku. ク is two strokes. ケ has a line across instead of the hook, with a stroke falling from its middle. タ is ク with one more short stroke inside.

drill.label: Read the kana
why: ケ is ke. ク is two strokes. ケ has a line across instead of the hook, with a stroke falling from its middle. タ is ク with one more short stroke inside.
